chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about a man who designated his female slave as a sacrificial offering (hady) for the Kaaba, asking what he should do. He said: 'My father received a man who had designated his female slave as a hady for the Kaaba, so he said: 'Order a crier to stand on the Hajar (stone) and announce: 'O you whose wealth has fallen short, or whose supply has been cut off, or whose food has run out, let him come to so-and-so son of so-and-so.' And he ordered him to give [from her value] first by first until the price of the female slave is exhausted.'

key_terms.الْحِجْر: The Hajar (a specific area near the Kaaba)
key_terms.ثَمَنُ الْجَارِيَةِ: The price of the female slave

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for redeeming a female slave designated as a hady for the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on expiation for the unintentional violation of Ihram restrictions details the specific procedure for redeeming a female slave dedicated as a *hady* to the Kaaba. Following the precedent set by Imam al-Sadiq’s father, Imam al-Baqir, the ruling mandates a public auction-style redemption where individuals with limited means are prioritized, ensuring the slave's value is gradually paid off until she is fully freed. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on accessibility and gradual emancipation within the framework of sacrificial dedications.
